**Traffic Laws Overview – State of Texas** | Topic | Key Statutes / Regulations | Typical Penalties | |-------|---------------------------|-------------------| | **Speed Limits & Speed‑Related Violations** | *Tx. Transp. Code § 545.001* (speed limit signs)
*§ 545.002* (maximum speed limits)
County/municipal ordinance variations | • Fine $50–$200 per violation
• Points added to driver’s record (1–2 pts)
• Possible license suspension if cumulative >12 pts within 36 months | | **Seat Belt Use** | *§ 545.021* (seat‑belt requirement) | • First offense fine $25 ($75 if child under 13 not buckled); second offense double fines; third offense up to $500 plus possible jail time | | **DUI/DWI** | *§ 549.031* (impaired driving)
*§ 549.032* (driving with blood alcohol concentration ≥0.08%) | • Initial fine $400+
• License revocation 90 days
• Mandatory ignition interlock device after first conviction | | **Texting While Driving** | *§ 545.041(a)(5)* (handheld electronic communication devices) | • Fine $100-$250 + 1 point | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | *§ 545.005* (right‑of‑way at intersections)
*§ 545.006* (yielding to pedestrians) | • Fines vary from $20–$150 depending on severity | | **School Bus Stop Signaling** | *§ 545.011* (school bus stop sign) | • Fine $300–$600; potential criminal charges if negligence causes injury | | **Commercial Vehicle Regulations** | *§ 544.* series (commercial motor vehicles)
*§ 546.* (truck weight limits) | • Varies widely—fines range from $200 to several thousand dollars; heavy truck oversize may lead to civil liability | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | *TxDOT Toll Road Authority Act* | • Violation results in automatic ticket sent to DMV; failure to pay leads to collection actions | | **Parking Restrictions** | Local city codes (e.g., Houston Parking Ordinance) | • Misdemeanor fines $30–$350; repeated offenses may result in towing | --- ### How Texas Handles Traffic Offenses 1. **Points System** - Each moving‑vehicle violation adds “points” to your Texas Driver Record. - Accumulating 12 or more points in a 36‑month period triggers a mandatory review and possible license suspension. - Certain serious infractions (e.g., DUIs) add 8–10 points automatically. 2. **Ticket Processing** - Most tickets are processed electronically via the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV). - You receive a notice detailing the charge, court appearance dates, and payment options. 3. **Court Appearance Options** - **Self‑Plead:** Pay the fine online or mail check before the deadline. - **Defend Yourself:** Attend scheduled hearing; you may present evidence or argue mitigating circumstances. - **Hire Representation:** A lawyer can negotiate plea bargains or represent you in court. 4. **License Suspension & Reinstatement** - Suspensions due to points or DUIs require completion of required courses (e.g., Alcohol Education Program) and sometimes a reinstatement fee. - For commercial drivers, additional licensing requirements apply (e.g., CDL reissuance). --- ### Recent Legislative Updates (as of 2024) | Update | Summary | Effective Date | |--------|---------|---------------| | **“Safe Streets Initiative”** | Reduced maximum penalty for minor speeding violations (<15 mph over limit). | Jan 1 2025 | | **Electronic Ignition Interlocks** | Expanded eligibility criteria for installing interlock devices post‑conviction. | Mar 31 2025 | | **Mobile Device Law Amendment** | Clarified definitions of “hands‑free” vs. “hand‑hold”; increased enforcement focus on distracted driving. | Jun 30 2025 | *(Check the Texas Legislature Online portal for full text.)* --- ### Resources for Further Information | Resource | What It Offers | Link | |----------|-----------------|------| | **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** | Official driver records, traffic safety statistics, educational materials | https://www.dps.texas.gov | | **Texas Highway Patrol** | Enforcement guidelines, public service announcements | https://www.txdhhs.state.tx.us/highwayspatrol | | **TX DOT – Traffic Management Division** | Current road conditions, construction updates, toll rates | https://www.transportation.gov/txtx | | **Legislature Online – Texas Senate Bill Tracker** | Bills affecting transportation policy | https://capitol.texas.gov/billtrack | | **Local City Codes** | Municipal parking, street cleaning schedules, special event permits | Usually available through each city’s official website (search “[City] code” e.g., “Houston municipal code”) | --- #### Quick Tips for Staying Compliant 1. **Always Observe Posted Signs** – Speed limits, turn lanes, and temporary detours change frequently during construction. 2. **Use Hands‑Free Devices Only When Necessary** – Even hands‑free calls count as “distraction” if you’re not fully focused on driving. 3. **Keep Your Records Updated** – If you move across counties, ensure your address is current so notices reach you promptly. 4. **Attend All Court Dates** – Missing a hearing can trigger default judgments and further legal complications. 5. **Consider Defensive Driving Courses** – Completing a certified course often reduces points and lowers insurance premiums.
